blocks.text: The first days focus on colonial Antigua and present-day Maya communities. The route then passes through the highlands and Lake Atitlán to the great Chichicastenango market. During the second half of the journey, archaeological sites become the main focus: Copán in Honduras, followed by Quiriguá and Tikal in Guatemala.\n\nThis itinerary traces Maya culture across different periods. Antigua and Iximché bring the history of the early capitals and the Spanish conquest into view. At Lake Atitlán, you encounter living Tz'utujil traditions, weaving, natural dyes, fishing and farming. Chichicastenango reveals the commercial and religious life of the highland communities. Copán, Quiriguá and Tikal offer a window into the Classic Maya period through monumental architecture, carved stelae and inscriptions.
